scope: Actual SU(2) Wilson normalized physical transfer response is bounded by its actual stationary variance dissipation, with no observable-range factor. For a rotation R_q at a specified link, B(beta,q)=(exp(4*beta*norm(q-1))-1)^2 and E_q(F)=E_pi|F(R_q u)-F(u)|^2, the proof gives E_q(P f)<=B*(Var_pi(f)-Var_pi(P f)). Iteration yields sum_{j<k} E_q(P^(j+1) f)<=B*(Var_pi(f)-Var_pi(P^k f))<=B*Var_pi(f), summability and vanishing response, and a 1/k time-average bound. The actual raw transition preserves the constructed ground law; on gauge-invariant observables all iterates are explicitly identified with powers of the original normalized complex Hilbert-space transfer under the ground-state embedding. The coefficient is independent of spatial volume and bounded by (exp(4)-1)^2 when beta*norm(q-1)<=1, but grows exponentially at fixed nonzero displacement as beta increases. Conditional one-step and whole-slab collective coercivity give variance contraction C/(1+C), C=sum_i weights_i*B(beta,q_i); their lower-bound premises are not proved. This does not establish a uniform physical gap, a surviving continuum source or a continuum limit. All twelve Clay obligations remain open.

proof.law: pi(du)=g(u)^2 Haar(du) for the already constructed strictly positive normalized ground amplitude; nu_u is the actual temporal-gauge transition row law.
proof.likelihood: The actual row densities satisfy p_u(v)<=exp(4*beta*inputCost(u,w))*p_w(v). For w=R_q u, inputCost is exactly norm(q-1). Both ratio directions imply |p_w/p_u-1|<=exp(4*beta*norm(q-1))-1.
proof.conditional_variance: Centering against nu_u and L2 Cauchy-Schwarz give |E_nu_w f-E_nu_u f|^2<=B(beta,q)*Var_nu_u(f). No range bound on f occurs.
proof.stationarity: Actual raw detailed balance and row normalization imply E_pi(P_raw f)=E_pi f for every continuous real f.
proof.variance_loss: E_pi Var_nu_u(f)=Var_pi(f)-Var_pi(P_raw f). Therefore E_q(P_raw f)<=B(beta,q)*(Var_pi(f)-Var_pi(P_raw f)).
proof.physical_identification: For gauge-invariant f, P_raw preserves gauge invariance and agrees with the original full ground-state-transformed transfer. embed(g*P_raw^k f)=normalizedTransfer^k embed(g*f) is proved for every natural k.
proof.infinite_time: The nonnegative response sequence is summable; its infinite sum is at most B*Var_pi(f), its terms tend to zero, and its k-step average is at most B*Var_pi(f)/k for k>0.
proof.scaling: If beta*norm(q-1)<=1 then B(beta,q)<=(exp(4)-1)^2. This controls individual shrinking rotations, not a collective Poincare constant.
proof.conditional_slab_payoff: If Var_pi(P^k f)<=sum_i w_i sum_{j<k} E_{e_i,q_i}(P^(j+1) f), with w_i>=0, then Var_pi(P^k f)<=C/(1+C)*Var_pi(f), where C=sum_i w_i B(beta,q_i). There is no additional factor k. The same implication is proved for one step. The collective lower-bound premise remains open.

assumptions: Finite periodic spatial SU(2) lattice n>0; beta>=0.
Continuous real observables, arbitrary chosen link and unit quaternion rotation.
Gauge invariance is required for the explicit original physical transfer identification; raw row-law variance and response statements hold for all continuous real observables.
The contraction theorems assume their displayed collective coercivity inequalities; these inequalities are not derived.
comparison_to_predecessor: The preceding bound 66*beta*range(f)^2*norm(q-1)^2 remains a separate estimate. The present bound uses actual variance loss, with coefficient (exp(4*beta*norm(q-1))-1)^2; no 66*beta variance-loss bound is claimed.
not_inferred: Prove collective coercivity under the actual squared-ground law: the variance after a fixed physical slab must be bounded by a suitable nonnegative weighted sum of its time-integrated local responses, with C=sum_i weights_i*(exp(4*beta*norm(q_i-1))-1)^2 uniformly controlled in cutoff and spatial volume for all physical observables.

The proved response upper bound and time summability alone give no rate of stationary variance decay. Shrinking rotations with beta*norm(q-1)<=1 do not by themselves control the collective coercivity constant or establish a physical scale.
